version.changelog: v0.5.1: 完整 P2P 通信系统 - 包含留言审批、离线同步、心跳机制

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: agent-p2p
Version: 0.5.1

The skill implements a decentralized P2P communication system that requires high-privilege operations, including remote VPS deployment via SSH and modification of local OpenClaw configuration files (install.py, setup.sh). It features an automated handshake mechanism in client.py that uses regex to extract tokens and verification codes from incoming messages, which then triggers outbound HTTP POST requests to URLs parsed directly from those messages, creating a potential SSRF or unauthorized data disclosure risk. Furthermore, the deployment script (deploy_portal.py) sets a hardcoded default password ('AgentP2P2024') for the portal's admin interface, and the system relies on pulling code from an external GitHub repository during setup.

llm.summary: The skill largely matches a P2P Portal/bridge purpose but has several mismatches and risky behaviors (undocumented required env, auto-deploy scripts that need SSH keys, token extraction/automatic confirmation logic, and hardcoded secrets) that you should review before installing or providing credentials.

dimensions.detail: The code and documentation implement a Portal + local Bridge + client capable of P2P messaging and VPS deployment, which aligns with the stated purpose. However the registry metadata claims no required environment variables while SKILL.md and many code paths require AGENTP2P_API_KEY, AGENTP2P_HUB_URL, OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_URL and OPENCLAW_HOOKS_TOKEN — a metadata/instruction mismatch that could mislead users about required credentials.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions and code do more than just connect over WebSocket: the client automatically polls guest messages, extracts verification codes and tokens from arbitrary message content, performs automatic verification confirmation by POSTing to other portals, and wakes the OpenClaw gateway with message contents. That automatic parsing/confirmation/extraction of secrets extends the skill's runtime scope beyond passive message relay and can surface or transmit sensitive tokens and codes without explicit user action.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The registry lists no install spec, but the package includes install.py and scripts/deploy_portal.py that perform remote deployment via SSH (paramiko) to the user's VPS, configure systemd, install packages, and write files. This is consistent with a deployable Portal product but is higher-risk than an instruction-only skill because it expects to run commands that change a remote system and may install dependencies automatically.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requires sensitive inputs: an API Key for the Portal, the user's OpenClaw hooks token (used to call /hooks/wake), and for deployment the user's SSH private key. Those are reasonable for the described Portal use, but the metadata did not declare them. Additionally the code extracts tokens from messages and may display/send parts of them via OpenClaw notifications, which could leak credentials if provided to untrusted peers.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and model-invocation is allowed (default). Locally the skill writes state/notification files under the user's home (~/.openclaw or ~/.agent_p2p*), runs a background bridge/client process, and the deployment scripts create a systemd service on the remote VPS. It does not appear to modify other skills' configs, but its background runtime and remote service setup give it lasting presence.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
Things to consider before installing:

- Metadata mismatch: the skill package actually expects environment variables (AGENTP2P_API_KEY, AGENTP2P_HUB_URL, OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_URL, OPENCLAW_HOOKS_TOKEN) though the registry lists none. Don't assume the skill needs no secrets.

- Sensitive credentials: you will be asked (or the code will read) your OpenClaw hooks token and Portal API Key. The hooks token lets the skill post to your OpenClaw gateway (/hooks/wake) and thus surface content to the main session. Only provide it if you trust the skill and its author.

- Deployment requires SSH private key access to a VPS: install.py/scripts will SSH as root/ubuntu and install services. Only run these if you control the VPS and are comfortable the script will make those changes; prefer manual review or running in a disposable VM first.

- Automatic token handling and auto-confirmation: the client code parses arbitrary message text to extract verification codes and tokens and can POST confirmations to third-party portals. This automation can cause secrets (tokens) to be collected and relayed; review or disable that behavior if you need stricter control.

- Hardcoded secret on remote service: the deployment writes a SECRET_KEY value into the systemd environment on the server. Change defaults and rotate secrets after deployment.

- Recommended precautions: review the source (especially client.py, install.py, scripts/deploy_portal.py, and any network POST/notification code), run the installer in a sandbox or on a throwaway VPS first, do not share central/privileged tokens unless necessary, change default admin credentials, and consider limiting network exposure (firewall, IP allowlist) for the Portal.

If you want, I can point to the exact code lines that extract tokens, auto-confirm codes, create systemd service, and call the OpenClaw hooks so you can inspect or patch them before use.
